checks.name: Offline local HTML initializes an actual 3D viewer
Trial-layout step disables the unnecessary exploded-view slider
Every mechanical step has rendered triangle meshes; wiring step remains a readable diagram
Pointer picking identifies visible model geometry
Mouse drag rotates the actual camera and changes rendered pixels
Mouse wheel zoom changes viewing distance
Exploded view moves individual parts and fasteners rather than only the percentage label
Hardware filter hides actual screw and nut meshes
Small screws can be selected, identified, isolated, focused and restored
Top, bottom and isometric camera controls point in their stated directions
Complete assembly matches the current independently visible component count and shell filtering reveals internals
Overview explosion moves the intended components and returning to the step resets its view
Step illustration and interactive 3D modes can be switched without losing the step
Enlarged model dialog restores the live 3D view to the step on closing
Mobile one-finger gesture rotates the 3D view
Mobile two-finger pinch zoom changes camera distance
Mobile controls and part selector fit within a 390px viewport
Unavailable WebGL automatically retains the diagram and functioning assembly navigation
All tested contexts run offline without external requests or uncaught script exceptions

scope: Interactive 3D viewing and responsive/offline behavior; not physical assembly validation.
